newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: JCI granted Mozambique coal option - paper.
newsitem.headline: JCI granted Mozambique coal option - paper.

text.p: The Mozambique government has granted South African mining house JCI Ltd a 120-day option to lead manage the development of a $1.5 billion coking coal project in central Mozambique, Business Day said on Friday.

The newspaper quoted a JCI Projects manager as saying the mining house had acquired the option in early December from the government, in conjunction with Mozambican mining company Yugo Africa, to investigate the potential of developing the Moatize coal fields.
Coal reserves at the site, 60 percent of which are coking coal, are estimated to be 2.2-billion tonnes, with projections of coal exports at seven million to 10 million tonnes a year, the paper said.

Keith Atkins, business development projects manager, said the option agreement required JCI to bring in other partners. Potential partners include Gencor Ltd, Ingwe Coal Corp Ltd and Brazil's Companhia do Vale Rio Doce, the world's third largest mining group, Business Day said.
Another possible partner was British Petroleum, although Atkins said he did not think the U.K group was interested.
Preliminary and final feasibility studies could take as long as two years, with the project possibly not starting up for four years, the paper quoted Atkins as saying.
